answer:
I opened `/home/hyoklee/cae_test_data/porotomo/dasv_native_PoroTomo_iDAS025_160318160317.h5` read-only and ran a full structure analysis on the root group (the file has no subgroups, so all 8 datasets sit at `/`). Here is every dataset with its shape and dtype, as read from the file:

| Dataset (path) | Shape | Dtype |
|---|---|---|
| `/channel` | (384,) | int32 |
| `/crs` | () (scalar) | uint8 |
| `/das` | (30000, 384) | float32 |
| `/t` | (30000,) | float64 |
| `/trace` | (30000,) | int64 |
| `/x` | (384,) | float32 |
| `/y` | (384,) | float32 |
| `/z` | (384,) | float32 |

Key points about this native DAS record:

- **`/das`** is the main strain-rate array: 30,000 time samples × 384 channels, float32 (~46 MB in memory). That is the dataset any anomaly/detection work would read — never the whole thing at once; use partial reads.
- **`/t`** (float64, 30,000) is the time axis for the 30,000 samples, and **`/trace`** (int64, 30,000) is the trace/sequence index.
- **`/channel`, `/x`, `/y`, `/z`** (384 each) are the channel number and the spatial coordinates of the 384 sensing points along the fiber.
- **`/crs`** is a scalar uint8 (coordinate reference system flag).

Source: structure analysis of the file itself via `hdf5_analyze_dataset_structure` after opening it read-only — no contents inferred from the filename. The file is now closed.
